column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3c and WORDS, tests GOLDMINE 30 and H7-067 at source: a bought deal is bought because it has no market-out (Bortolotti et al. 2008 re-read at source by the rater, with over 90% Canadian and about 20 days to resell); the exact finance word for the range after the move, if one is used.

Thu 19 Nov: WORDS guard for 3c: Rule 10b-9(b) re-read at source by the rater (a firm commitment subject only to customary conditions precedent, including market outs), so never call the stated range a firm commitment; the gloss is 'nothing in markets can change it', never 'nothing can' (row 40).
Thu 19 Nov: store, an illustration for row 2: what an ordinary market-out lists (trading halts, any change in financial markets); a two-day out against a statement held about two years.
Thu 19 Nov: the row says it adds no idea beyond H6-001; carry FINRA 16-08's wording there as the citable regulator's definition of best efforts and firm commitment.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d, pairs with Q11c and Q147: a pledge if the total is reached is a best-efforts contingency, Laura's own stated figure is not one.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; about 1 in 4 best-efforts IPOs withdrawn (1980-84) is read at source but rests on tiny issuers, nothing like co-sponsors, and 3c has no room for it.

Thu 19 Nov: store; abstract only, so S 4; drop the inference that co-sponsors give more against an owned figure, since riskier firms chose best efforts (the row's own critique); cite only the 21.22% against 31.87% cost gap.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; abstract only; Smith calls the choice of underwriters hard to justify, so never cite him as showing a promisee values certainty above its cost.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c spine row 'speaking early does', at source: underwriting is valued as a put written to the issuer (BoE WP 39), so a top stated before the move is a put written to co-sponsors for nothing, priced by NUMBERS 4 (2.9% to 10.6%, checked); say simulated futures in prose; pairs with H8-033.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c support for row 9: the City billed the window by the week (0.125% per week past thirty days), the same shape as NUMBERS 4's rising shortfall by month (checked); one clause at most beside row 9.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c reasoning, kills claim 1: underwriters win on average even counting 1987, because they spread it over many deals for a fee and Laura has one; say 1986-93, not seven years; Marsh 1994 not opened.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; the 7% IPO spread is custom as much as risk and does no job in a part.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; one 2025 deal's spread (4.0%) and option size (15.0%) check against the schedule as stated.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; the greenshoe short is covered by its option, so the contrast with Laura is weak; the row rightly keeps the ban on a stated contribution above the stated top.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3c's reasoning: banks run bought deals for clients and league tables, reasons Laura does not have; journalism, not data.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3c's reasoning (a bank absorbs 1 bad deal in 20 because it has the other 19); read through a page extract and an unnamed banker's estimate, never a rate.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c reasoning: the risk is not removed, only placed, and before the move it sits on which range she can announce (NUMBERS 4, checked); cite only once the original Bloomberg column and its author are read.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; Vivendi and ENEL show a short window is not a safe one, but BP 1987 carries that job for 3c.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d beside Q147 and the funder test: the form of a promise signals quality; abstract only, and Laura's form is a rule, not a choice of issue.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c's real event for why nothing is stated before the move: BP priced two weeks before trading and fell about a fifth in that fortnight (330p to 262p is -20.6%, checked); date it 'underwritten on 15 October' as Hansard does.
Thu 19 Nov: store; clause 8's text was not read, and 'releasing it is not hers to decide' overstates: case l.114 makes the cost of not meeting a stated figure her credibility, not a contract.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d: Lawson's 'from that moment' line is strong, but say co-sponsors count a stated figure from the moment it is said (funder test), never that it belongs to them or that they hold her to it (the row's own disanalogy).
Thu 19 Nov: 3c sizing for the BP story: the public took about 3.2% and the promisers about 93.7% (71m and 2,055m of 2,194m, checked); whoever promised a fixed figure paid.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3c: UK sub-underwriting spread the risk, North America's did not; Laura has no sub-underwriters, so an early top would rest on her alone.
Thu 19 Nov: store; contemporary press estimates of the US firms' BP losses (final figures not found); Goldman's own page for the largest underwriting loss.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; CONFLICTING (Hansard 0.018% against IFR's 18bp, a tenfold gap), so resolve at source before any fee figure, and drop the rough 1% for two weeks against 20%.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c guard and aha, kills claim 3: Hansard 27 May 1988 re-read at source by the rater (38,576,002 part-paid shares, scheme closed 6 Jan), about 1.8% of 2,126m; the floor sat 50p under what the banks paid, so never 'the floor bailed them out'.
Thu 19 Nov: store beside row 27: the state's 70p put was cheap because it was struck far below; the £1bn is an MP's arithmetic, not an official estimate.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; the part-paid share's -41.7% against the full share's -20.6% checks, but the link to Laura is loose.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; the Kuwait Investment Office's post-crash stake does no job in a part.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED past the paywalled lead paragraph, and the Australian angle earns no place in the report.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c's one line on why she states only what she owns: 'You can only do that if it is a risk you can deal with'; quoted in IFR (2013) years later, so cite IFR and the speaker's role at the time.
Thu 19 Nov: 3c reasoning: HM Treasury's own cure was to fix the price after the money is known, the order Laura's rule keeps; never say BP caused it (the guide names the 1990 sale).
Thu 19 Nov: store, a second case for 3c's window (57 days, 8.29% take-up); BP carries the job, and the HBOS banks had sub-underwritten much of it.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the FSA's cut to 14 days was read only as a January 2009 proposal and a trade blog, so say proposed until the final rule is read; the fee rise to 3.4% is read at source.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d reasoning: the law polices a certainty word (all-or-none) only with a refund mechanism behind it (Rule 10b-9(a) re-read by the rater); her bottom as the minimum held first, never 'escrow' or 'escrowed' for her holdings (H1-015).

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3c; 'what the funds pay' must become what the late-2032 fund pays on its two purchases (one fund bought twice, NUMBERS 4's one definition); spending from her flexibility stays her separate choice outside the range (CANON D12).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d client knowledge: Taiwan's securities law already names the two promises (包銷 must buy what is unsold, 代銷 may hand it back); in the report's analysis only, never in Laura's words to co-sponsors (voice round 8).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d candidate, but art. 81's multiple was not read, so never say Taiwan lets a bank promise more than it holds or call Laura's rule the strictest version of its test until the regulator's figure is read; the cap is set against net current assets, not the promised securities.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and WORDS, checked against NUMBERS 3 and 4: a window remains after the move, fund mechanics not price ($4,589 at worst with waiting cash at zero, nothing short at today's market rates); never 'no window' or 'nothing can'; NUMBERS 3 shows the gap grows with the exit-day yield, so 'nothing in markets' holds only absent a fund event; 3e's plain line is 'No fall in share prices can.'

Thu 19 Nov: misreads NUMBERS 8o: of the $5,300 about $5,000 is money moved into the promise, and her total barely moves (median $365), so certainty's price is small, not the growth the moved half gives up; say co-sponsors pay no spread and Laura chooses the split.

Thu 19 Nov: store, or a clause in 3c if a judge asks why the top is rounded down: the room under the top is about 2%, in all, of what the late-2032 fund pays on its two purchases (WORDS), never a year, on a different base from a banker's discount.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3e or 3d: a syndicate writes a member falling short into its contract (one-eleventh), as IPS l.15 names a co-sponsor falling short as one use of her flexibility, which is sized to no fraction and owed to no one.
